mainText:
Good morning, it's Saturday, Sept. 19.

President Donald Trump to ban CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from White House.
Trump said yesterday that the outlets were being banned for reporting what he characterized as fake news. He warned bans on other outlets would follow, but did not specify which or when. Trump has previously attempted to take legal action against the BBC, the New York Times, and the Wall Street Journal, and banned the Associated Press from the Oval Office, Air Force One, and other events.
Pentagon releases sixth batch of UFO files, details secret military program.
Yesterday's drop comprises 71 files dating from 1952 to 2025 (
see here
). Several documents examine a secretive military initiative that ran from 2008 to 2012 to anticipate future aerospace threats. The memos explore the possibility of
warp drives
, wormholes, antigravity, negative mass propulsion, and invisibility cloaking. Another document details unintended injury to humans by anomalous advanced aerospace systems, including hair loss and signs of cancerous cell growth.
Russia begins voting in first wartime parliamentary elections.
Russia yesterday began voting in parliamentary elections that are all but assured to keep the country's ruling United Russia party in power. The election includes residents of four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the war began, as well as Crimea. The only political entity that opposes the invasion of Ukraine—the Yabloko party—was removed from the ballot last month by Russia's Supreme Court.
Three dead, several wounded in Philippine high school shooting.
A 16-year-old killed two peers, both 14, before taking his own life yesterday; at least eight others were wounded. The shooter was reportedly part of an online "true crimes community," and the gun belonged to his father. This is the third school shooting since June in the Philippines, where such attacks had previously been rare. Experts cite a rise in depression among youth and relaxing gun laws.
Philadelphia police and FBI investigate serial murders at "house of horrors."
Officials this week tied a Philadelphia home to at least seven missing women, five of whom are presumed dead. Police began investigating the home this summer after arresting its owner, 44-year-old Eugene Horsch, on drug, firearm, and forged document charges. The property search uncovered over 1 million digital images, including many of women reported missing for over a decade.
Tony- and Grammy-winning composer Duncan Sheik dies at age 56.
Sheik died in Manhattan of heart failure leading to cardiac arrest, his representatives said yesterday. The composer is best known for his 1996 debut song, "Barely Breathing" (
listen here
). He went on to write the music for the coming-of-age rock musical "Spring Awakening," which premiered on Broadway in 2006. He won the Grammy for best musical theater album and two music-related Tonys.
Scientists discover a new "baby" planet.
Astronomers this week confirmed the existence of a planet 450 light-years from Earth that is less than 1 million years old, the youngest planet on record. The planet, Elias 2-24 b, was discovered in old data archives and is nearly the size of Jupiter, the largest planet in our solar system. The previous youngest known planet was over 5 million years old.
